summary: Checkout p99 latency tripled with no error-rate change and no deploy in the window. Vigil declined to name a culprit: the strongest candidate reached 0.35 confidence against a 0.4 floor. The brief carried three ranked candidates and the dashboard triage path instead.

timeline.event: Three changes touching the payment path merged within 40 minutes of each other.
LatencyBudgetBurn alert fired for checkout (p99 2.4s against a 780ms baseline).
Vigil brief posted: no culprit named, three candidates ranked with rationales, dashboards-and-logs runbook cited.
Incident marked resolved after the batching window was lowered and p99 returned to budget.

root_cause: Most likely the 250ms batching window added to authorize_all in libs/payments/batch.py, compounded by doubled worker concurrency against unchanged downstream pool limits. The evidence available during the incident did not establish a single cause, and the automated analysis reported that rather than guessing.
contributing_factors: Three latency-relevant changes landed in the same window with no deploy markers to separate them.
The batching window was introduced with no latency budget check in CI.
impact: No requests failed; checkout p99 ran at 2.4s against a 780ms baseline, burning the latency budget roughly 6x for the duration.
resolution: Lowered the batching window to 50ms, which returned p99 to 900ms. The concurrency change was left in place and is being monitored.
went_well: The confidence floor prevented a plausible-sounding but unproven root cause from being stated as fact.
On-call still received ranked candidates with per-feature scores, so triage started from evidence rather than from scratch.
went_poorly: Latency-affecting changes ship without deploy events, so deploy correlation contributed nothing here.
No p99 regression gate exists in CI for the payment path.

action_items.description: Emit deploy events for config and library changes so latency incidents get deploy correlation too.
Add a p99 budget check to the payment path in CI.
Document the batching window as a tunable with its latency cost in the checkout runbook.
